涙.meaning: A clown's job is to make children laugh, but every autumn, when the circus has to <part>return</part> to its winter barn, <part>water drops</part> squirt from the flower on his jacket and run down his painted cheeks. The children think it's a trick. It isn't. Those are real <kanji>tears</kanji>.
涙.on: The barn is nearly an old <sound>rui</sound>n, with a hole where the roof should be.
涙.kun: He shares warm <sound>na</sound>an with a <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a <sound>du</sound>ck, who sniffle along with him.

盾.meaning: A nervous goalkeeper practises at the foot of a <part>cliff</part>. Rocks bounce down; he counts to <part>ten</part>, peeks out with one <part>eye</part> from behind an old saucepan lid, and every rock clangs off it. He has never saved a ball, but he's found the perfect <kanji>shield</kanji>.
盾.on: Between rockfalls, he leans the lid against a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to rest his arm.
盾.kun: He hides under it to eat a <sound>ta</sound>co in his little <sound>te</sound>nt.

械.meaning: A bossy park ranger bolts a gadget into an old <part>tree</part>: cogs, pulleys and a loudspeaker that barks each park <part>commandment</part> at passers-by. No picnics, no ball games, no fun. Then a squirrel jams an acorn in the gears and it squeaks to a halt. So much for his <kanji>contraption</kanji>.
械.on: Before it broke, its grabbing arm caught a child's <sound>ki</sound>te and wouldn't let go.
械.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp from the pond flops up and <sound>se</sound>ts the kite free.

鉛.meaning: A clumsy alchemist tries to turn grey slop into <part>gold</part> by pouring it through a magic <part>funnel</part>. He gets it backwards: his gold ring slips in, and out drips something dull, soft and so heavy it falls through the floor. He has invented <kanji>lead</kanji>.
鉛.on: It lands with a clunk on the <sound>en</sound>gine of the car in his cellar.
鉛.kun: His neighbour uses the flat lump to press <sound>na</sound>an for her <sound>ma</sound>ma and to sink a fishing line by the <sound>ree</sound>f.

厄.meaning: A grumpy postman lives in a hut under a <part>cliff</part>. Every letter that crosses his desk gets a big red <part>stamp</part> of a broken mirror. Whoever opens one trips on the stairs, loses a sock and gets rained on. Nobody in town wants to be that <kanji>unlucky</kanji>.
厄.on: He keeps one spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca on his counter, and it pricks everyone who reaches for their mail.

粋.meaning: A tiny café at a crossroads has no shop sign, just a wooden <part>signpost</part> wearing a silk scarf and sunglasses, one arm pointing at a bowl of plain <part>rice</part> on the doorstep. Fashion models queue round the block. Plain rice has never looked so <kanji>chic</kanji>.
粋.on: Each bowl comes with one wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t balanced on top.
粋.kun: The doorman is an <sound>ee</sound>l in a bow tie, with a gold <sound>key</sound> round his neck.

翼.meaning: An inventor glues <part>feathers</part> to two old doors, a <part>different</part> kind on each: pigeon on the left, peacock on the right. He leaps off the barn and flies in circles all afternoon, fast and very lopsided. Next time he'll match each <kanji>wing</kanji>.
翼.on: He lands face first in a frying pan, with egg <sound>yo</sound>lk on his nose.
翼.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', blowing feathers across the <sound>ba</sound>rn and into a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

稚.meaning: A young <part>sparrow</part> is put in charge of guarding the farm's <part>grain</part> from the other birds. Instead he eats it, throws it at the hens and sulks when the scarecrow won't play tag with him. The farmer sighs. Still far too <kanji>immature</kanji> for the job.
稚.on: Next he dares a <sound>chee</sound>tah at the zoo to a race, and loses before he flaps once.
稚.kun: He cheeps '<sound>Ee</sound>!' at a <sound>to</sound>rch, pecks a <sound>ke</sound>ttle, steals the farmer's <sound>na</sound>an and cheeps '<sound>Ee</sound>!' again.
